label: Lesson 41
titleEn: Do You Call That a Hat?

lines.en: What kind of shopping does the writer enjoy, do you think?
lines.cn: 你觉得这位作家喜欢哪种类型的购物呢？

lines.en: 'Do you call that a hat?' I said to my wife.
lines.cn: “你那叫帽子吗？”我对我的妻子说道。

lines.en: 'You needn't be so rude about it,'
my wife answered as she looked at herself in the mirror.
lines.cn: 我妻子一边看着镜子中的自己，一边回答了我。

lines.en: I sat down on one of those modern chairs with holes in it and waited.
lines.cn: 我坐在那把带有孔洞的现代风格椅子上，然后等待着。

lines.en: We had been in the hat shop for half an hour and my wife was still in front of the mirror.
lines.cn: 我们在那家帽子店已经待了半个小时了，而我妻子仍然站在镜子前挑选帽子。

lines.en: 'We mustn't buy things we don't need,' I remarked suddenly.
lines.cn: “我们不应该购买那些我们不需要的东西，”我突然说道。

lines.en: I regretted saying it almost at once.
lines.cn: 我几乎立刻就后悔说了那句话。

lines.en: 'You needn't have said that,' my wife answered.
lines.cn: “你其实没必要那么说，”我的妻子回答道。

lines.en: 'I needn't remind you of that terrible tie you bought yesterday.'
lines.cn: “我其实没必要再提醒你昨天你买的那条糟糕的领带了。”

lines.en: 'I find it beautiful,' I said. 'A man can never have too many ties.'
lines.cn: “我觉得这很漂亮，”我说，“一个男人永远都不应该拥有太少的领带。”

lines.en: 'And a woman can't have too many hats,' she answered.
lines.cn: “而且，一个女人永远都不嫌帽子戴得太多，”她回答道。

lines.en: Ten minutes later we walked out of the shop together.
lines.cn: 十分钟后，我们一起走出了那家商店。

lines.en: My wife was wearing a hat that looked like a lighthouse!
lines.cn: 我妻子戴着一顶看起来像灯塔的帽子！
